resources.string: These steps use the calculator’s parsed inputs and formula, not AI. Decimal arithmetic uses finite precision; the main result may display fewer digits.
Convert the percentage: %1$s ÷ 100 = %2$s.\nMultiply by the value: %2$s × %3$s = %4$s.
The original value is a signed denominator. Negative starting values can reverse the usual increase/decrease interpretation.
The original price is zero. This calculator reports a 0% effective discount rather than dividing by zero.
Parsed ratio: %1$s : %2$s.\nMultiply both terms by 10^%3$d to obtain whole numbers: %4$s : %5$s.
Greatest common divisor of the absolute whole-number terms: %1$s.
The decimal representation comes from parsed floating-point values; digits already lost during input parsing cannot be recovered.
